name: Production error masking for server actions

arm-01.note: This codebase has zero Next.js Server Actions ('use server') anywhere -- all mutations go through API routes, so the item's literal subject doesn't exist in this architecture. In practice, thrown ActionError instances carry developer-curated safe messages surfaced via `error.message` in ~17 route catch blocks (all staff-permission-gated already), and genuinely unexpected exceptions fall through to Next's default production error handling (masked to the client, logged server-side) since no custom catch-all wrapper was found. Adequate by convention, not by a dedicated masking mechanism.

arm-04.note: Identical pattern; no functional diff in this batch's touched files.

arm-05.note: Also no Server Actions; API routes return `error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'fallback'` in several places with no dedicated typed-error-to-safe-message mapping layer observed, slightly less structured than the clone cluster's ActionError convention.

arm-06.note: No Server Actions either, but lib/errors.ts (typed NotFoundError/DomainRuleError) + lib/http-errors.ts's mapDomainError()/mapDomainErrorOrThrow() form a deliberate, reusable ladder: known domain errors map to safe messages + correct status codes, an optional `clientMessage` field lets a route show a staff-safe summary while logging the full detail server-side via console.error, and anything unrecognized is rethrown to Next's default (masked) handling. The most deliberately engineered error-masking layer of the batch, even though it targets API routes rather than literal server actions.
